Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + next steps (Acme)

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the model shortlist we recommend for your use case (customer support summarization + first-pass routing):

Goals you mentioned
- 95% intent classification accuracy on short messages (<= 256 tokens)
- Low-cost first-pass summarization for triage
- SLA: p95 latency <= 400ms for hosted API; dedicated option for stricter SLAs

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality)
1) Redwood-7B-quant (recommended starting point)
   - Rationale: lowest latency and cost; strong on templated summaries and routing for short prompts
   - Typical p95 latency (hosted): ~120-220ms; est cost: $8 / 1M tokens (inference-only)
   - When to pick: if volume is high and you need predictable low unit costs

2) Open-Mega-13B (balanced)
   - Rationale: better open-domain understanding and fewer hallucinations on long context; higher cost
   - Typical p95 latency (hosted): ~260-420ms; est cost: $22 / 1M tokens
   - When to pick: if you need better NLU and higher quality in ambiguous cases

3) Redwood-70B-ptq (highest quality, heavier)
   - Rationale: best for complex summarization and subtle intent classification; higher latency and cost, recommended for targeted fallback flows
   - Typical p95 latency (hosted): ~600-900ms; est cost: $95 / 1M tokens
   - When to pick: low-volume high-complexity paths, or as a fallback in canary/A/B rollouts

Next steps I propose:
- Run a warmup eval using the attached prompt set (acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl) against Redwood-7B-quant and Open-Mega-13B. We recommend 500 representative samples for an initial quality delta measurement.
- I uploaded a short benchmark PDF (redwood-benchmarks-acme.pdf) with sample latency/cost projections and hallucination scoring methodology. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/acme/benchmarks
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up the week of Nov 23 to review eval results and pick the PO/Proc path (hosted vs Dedicated).

If helpful, I can also put together a quick canary plan: start 90% traffic on Redwood-7B-quant + 10% fallback to Open-Mega-13B for the first 2 weeks to compare live metrics.

Attaching: redwood-benchmarks-acme.pdf, acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — great questions. Quick answers and links below: 

1) Hallucination metric
- Recommended metric: hallucination rate measured as % of summaries containing at least one verifiably incorrect statement relative to the source (binary label). For an initial eval we recommend a pass/fail threshold of <= 5% for the primary model.
- We included a small hallucination checklist in the attached benchmarks PDF and a spreadsheet in the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/acme/benchmarks

2) SLA differences
- Hosted API (standard): availability SLA 99.9% with p95 latency targets per model class (see attached PDF for measured p95s); suitable for most customers with fast time-to-value.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): availability SLA 99.95+ and network isolation — p95 latency targets tightened depending on instance type (we can commit to specific numbers in the SOW). Dedicated also supports burst pools for traffic spikes.

3) Pricing (ballpark)
- Hosted pay-as-you-go: as noted in the shortlist, per-1M-token inference ranges (approx): Redwood-7B-quant $8; Open-Mega-13B $22; Redwood-70B-ptq $95.
- Dedicated reserved (monthly commit): pricing depends on GPU class and commit term. Typical starting points: $12k–$25k/mo for a minimal Dedicated pool suitable for 3–5k qps of small prompts; larger pools scale up. I cc'd Dev to provide a tailored estimate and a procurement-friendly quote template.

Eval plan and immediate ask
- We suggest starting with 500 labeled samples from your corpus. Neha can run the eval in our sandbox and share a dashboard with token-level cost, latency distribution, and hallucination counts.
- Proposed follow-up times (30m): Nov 24 (10am or 2pm PT), Nov 25 (11am PT) — which works for you?

Links / attachments
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/acme/benchmarks
- Prompt set: https://docs.redwood.ai/prompt-sets/acme-v1 (attached acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl)
- Benchmark PDF: attached redwood-benchmarks-acme.pdf

Dev (cc) — can you drop a short dedicated pricing estimate and a minimal SOW snippet we can send to procurement?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the eval kickoff once you confirm the sample set.

Best,
Marissa
